method: Synthetic voice designed from a text description with Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign (Apache-2.0); the selected output is the ICL clone reference for the Base streaming workers.
rights: No human speaker recorded or cloned. Model weights Apache-2.0. Safe for synthetic use.
instruct: A male American speaker in his late thirties with a warm, calm, slightly low voice. He sounds like a friendly, patient insurance representative chatting on the phone with an older customer: relaxed, confident, approachable and a little casual, with natural conversational pacing. General American accent. Not an announcer, not a radio voice, not salesy or over-enthusiastic.
ref_text: Hey, how's it going? Yeah, so I'm just following up on that information you'd asked about. It's real simple, it only takes a minute. And honestly, if anything doesn't make sense, just stop me and I'll walk you through it.
post_processing: loudness-normalized +4.35 dB to -20 dBFS active-speech RMS (peak -4.4 dBFS), 16-bit PCM 24 kHz
selection_basis: objective screen of 6 candidates (see candidates/*.json): male register median F0 119 Hz, calm pitch movement 4.1 st, moderate pausing, 3.3 words/s, 0 WER at 24 kHz and 8 kHz mu-law. Final choice must be confirmed by ear.
regenerate: python -m tools.design_voice --model Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-VoiceDesign --out <dir> --instructs warm_rep --seeds 11 --device cpu --dtype float32 (seeded on CPU float32; GPU sampling differs)

conditioning.alex_fec_v1: x_vector_only_mode=true: speaker embedding of reference.wav. Chosen for bounded turn-start silence.
conditioning.alex_fec_v1_icl: ICL clone on reference_short.wav (last sentence of reference.wav, 8.1 s onward). Carries the reference's casual delivery; keep for by-ear A/B.
conditioning.measurement: 0.6B Base, 5 lines x 3 seeds, leading silence P50/max: x-vector 370/540 ms; short ICL 370/1040 ms; full 12.6 s ICL ~700/2210 ms. Speaker similarity to reference.wav ~0.965 for all.
